title: Start with Azure and Foundry
summary: Understand the purchasing assistant and choose a path matching your readiness.

title: Prepare your account, PC, and budget (Project / RBAC)
summary: Prepare your PC and check the instructor-supplied project and access.

title: Check the model you will use (Model Deployment)
summary: Confirm the supplied model, version, and cost conditions; save its actual deployment name.

title: Get your first answer from code (Responses API)
summary: Send one question through the Responses API and read the answer and response ID.

title: Create an agent with a clear role (Prompt Agent)
summary: Give a Prompt Agent rules, then compare the same conversation with a new one.

title: Answer from company documents (File search / RAG)
summary: Use File search to retrieve policies and inspect actual supporting evidence.

title: Check stock and prepare a draft (Function Calling / Capstone)
summary: Check inventory and amounts, then review the saved integrated result's evidence and pending-approval state in the same lab.

title: Connect tools with MCP and OpenAPI
summary: Retrieve the same inventory through local HTTP and MCP, with explicit call approval.

title: Compare answers and read scores (Evaluation)
summary: Read the instructions and questions; optionally compare your own v1/v2 answers, scores, and reasons.

title: Reject missing facts and false approval (Safety / Guardrails)
summary: Use three boundary questions to distinguish verbal refusal from actual function rejection.

title: Follow an answer's execution path (Tracing)
summary: Find a run's operations and durations in Traces to narrow latency and failure causes.

title: AI Search, Foundry IQ, and permission-aware retrieval
summary: Move beyond a few files to enterprise knowledge from multiple sources.

title: Hosted agents and developer tools
summary: Move your code and framework into a managed runtime.

title: Agent Framework: sequential and concurrent execution
summary: Review one purchasing question in sequence or divide it among independent roles, then compare actual inputs and outputs.

title: Agent Framework: group chat and handoff
summary: Run revision after review and specialist delegation separately; inspect actual messages, tool calls, and termination.

title: Memory: remembering and forgetting
summary: Separate conversation state from long-term memory and preserve user boundaries.

title: Routines, long-running agents, and Autopilot
summary: Distinguish scheduling, recovery, and the identity behind an execution.

title: Enterprise security, Control Plane, and gateways
summary: Design control boundaries across tenants, projects, tools, and data.

title: CI/CD: quality gates, publishing, and rollback
summary: An elective for deployment and operations owners. Repair a local promotion gate and design version selection, publishing, and recovery; live changes need separate approval.

title: Finish the lab and check costs (Cost Management)
summary: After core or selected advanced labs, record resource state, retention ownership, and the next cost-check time.

title: Troubleshooting by symptom
summary: Resolve 401, 403, 404, and 429 errors, empty search results, and unexpected costs.

title: Instructor plan and completion checklist
summary: Plan a 90-minute, one-day, or two-day workshop and record costs and outcomes.

title: Glossary and decision guide
summary: Clarify confusing names with short definitions and selection criteria.

title: Feature coverage
summary: See how official capability groups map to the labs.

title: Sources, currency, and execution boundaries
summary: Check official sources and distinguish execution from quality claims.
